messages:
anya: Hey team — customer reported intermittent mTLS handshake failures from their VPC to our private control plane since ~11:40 UTC. Symptoms: Client gets TLS alert handshake_failure, control-plane logs show 'client_hello parse error'. Only happens when egress goes through their corporate Squid/SSL-bump proxy.

matt: Can you paste the tcpdump + any openssl output we have? quick check: is SNI present or rewritten? :eyes:

anya: Snippet from their tcpdump (redacted):
```
14:05:12.123456 IP client > squid: TCP 1500
14:05:12.123457 IP squid > controlplane: TCP 536
14:05:12.123458 TLS ClientHello (fragment 1/3) len=512
14:05:12.123459 TLS ClientHello (fragment 2/3) len=256
14:05:12.123460 TLS ClientHello (fragment 3/3) len=128
14:05:12.123461 TLS Alert: handshake_failure (server->client)
```
Proxy appears to be chopping the ClientHello into multiple small records and reassembling/rewriting. They also see "squid SSL bump: inspecting" in proxy logs.

julia-netops: When Squid does SSL-Bump it terminates the TLS and re-originates to our host — that can change extensions or drop uncommon extensions. If the re-originated ClientHello is missing key extensions (e.g., session ticket, alpn) our control plane rejects because we require ALPN and certain keyshares for compatibility with our runtime.

anya: Customer tried allowlisting our FQDN `private-control.redwood.internal` but still fails. They said the proxy team does interception even for allowlisted hosts unless configured with `ssl_bump none` for that ACL.

matt: Two quick repro steps to ask them for: 1) from a host in their VPC: `openssl s_client -connect private-control.redwood.internal:443 -tlsextdebug -status` (no proxy). 2) same host but forcing traffic through their proxy (or from a host behind proxy) and capture the ClientHello bytes. Compare ClientHello length and extensions.

julia-netops: Also ask them to `tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/ch.pcap host private-control.redwood.internal` and check for any `TLS record length: 0` or multiple small TLS records. Squid/transparent proxies sometimes fragment TLS records which can break some servers expecting full ClientHello in a single handshake burst.

anya: They provided an openssl run via proxy: it shows SNI replaced with IP and missing ALPN. Example: `TLS server name: 10.2.3.45` instead of our hostname. That explains the parse error on our side.

matt: Ok — this is proxy doing SNI rewrite / hostname-to-ip. Workarounds: a) configure Squid to allow true CONNECT tunnel (no interception) for our control plane host/port, b) add their egress NAT range to an allowlist so traffic bypasses the intercepting proxy, or c) if org policy forbids bypass, have their proxy team configure `ssl_bump peek`/`splice` rules so the original ClientHello is forwarded.

julia-netops: I'll provide the control-plane IP ranges and cert thumbprints they can allowlist. Note: if they try allowlisting by DNS only, ensure the proxy doesn't rewrite DNS or do DNS-based interception. Recommend allowlisting by source egress IP -> destination IP/port.

anya: Customer asked for immediate temporary mitigation — asked for precise IP ranges and the server cert fingerprint. Can we ship those to them?

julia-netops: I'll DM the ops list with IP range `34.210.12.0/26` (example), port 443, and cert SHA256 `AB:12:CD:34:...` They should use those in their firewall/allowlist so proxy is bypassed.

anya: ticket updated with suggested repro steps and workarounds. Waiting on proxy team confirmation. Thanks all :pray:

sre-bot: ticket #3421 updated: assigned -> julia-netops; status -> needs-customer-action
